{{Quote|Over the centuries, Sith scribes simplified this system, creating several less complicated scripts from their hieroglyphic predecessor. While some supplemented the hieroglyphic writing to create the High Sith writing style for ecclesiastical uses, others such as the Common Sith script supplanted it in more mundane settings.|Doctor Milanda Vorgan, "The Written Word: A Brief Introduction to the Writing Systems of Galactic Basic"|<ref name="TWW">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/writtenword/index.html?page=1|text=The Written Word|int=The Written Word}}</ref>}}

'''High Sith''' was a script that stemmed from early [[hieroglyphics]] utilized by the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], created chiefly for ecclesiastical uses.
{{Stub}}

==History==
The Sith had developed writing in [[hieroglyphics|hiroglyphic]] form since the [[Pre-Republic era|Pre-Republic era]]. High Sith has been developed by Sith scribes who simplified this predecessor, although it was supplemented by original hieroglyphs for ritualistic uses. It coexisted with the related [[Common Sith]], which was less ornate and used in more everyday context.<ref name="TWW" />

After the fall of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]], and the use of the [[hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] by the Sith, their writing could be found in [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]], [[Jaguada/Legends|Jaguada]], even in [[Tund/Legends|Tund]] beyond [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith Space]].<ref name="TWW" />

Most Sith manuscripts that have been found were written in High Sith. Among them was [[Freedon Nadd]]'s [[Sith spellbook/Legends|Sith spellbook]].

Another Sith script, [[Massassi (alphabet)|Massassi]], was in use by the warrior class of the Sith species, and appeared etched on temple walls on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]; [[xenographologist]]s discovered that the Massassi alphabet had ties to the simplified component of High Sith writing.<ref name="TWW" />
